posts.name: Melkhor
posts.cooked:
Comfortable Mint for me here, with everyone up and in good condition (not counting the fact that Mainstay had been down three times but kept getting back up, of course!), though it certainly took a while. I always love a good La Capitan fight, and this one certainly didn't disappoint. Make sure to drop Mabel immediately, and the ship right afterwards and you should be right on track. Also, get Hippocratic Oath out as soon as possible, if you're going for the long slog, you'll definitely appreciate all the healing. Unity also really gets to shine in this one, as using Reconfigured Beebots to deal with La Capitan's horrible ongoings is the way to go.

I didn't actually use any of Parse's deck controlling powers, since Fugue State Parse's base power is just so incredibly good, especially once she has snap decision out.

posts.name: Yoshi348
posts.cooked:
Mint.

I fully expected to lose when I gambled on Syntactic Analysis on the Sentinels instead of just shooting Mable with an Impossible Shot, and lost showing no damage cards. Despite that, I managed to stabilize very well and was able to keep some great cards in play for pretty much the rest of the game, after an inital Plunder. Hippocratic Oath kept everyone alive through a LOT, Parse used her base power a lot but switch to deck control to toss some of the meaner cards left in the deck into the trash before the reshuffle, and my god constantly recurring Bee Bots are like, the best. They soak up so much damage and get rid or nullify so many nasty things between La Capitan and the enivornment; I took out the Pillars with them, absorbed Krakens, and stopped Defenses and Revenge from hitting the party. Expatriatte was gunless for longer than I'd have liked but she did eventually get her shotgun out. Dealing with all the crew members was a slog; I don't think I stuck any damage onto La Capitan herself until her deck had like 6 cards left, but I lived, and that's what matters.

posts.cooked: Easy mint for me.  Mabel and the ship have to go first, of course.  Expatriette served to provide sacrificial ongoings since it took her so long to draw a gun.  Took a gamble and left the Phosphorescent Chamber out pretty much the whole game, since my team was going far more damage and healing that La Capitan was, and it ultimately paid off.  Fugue State Parse is absolutely nuts, I really wish I'd been able to print-and-play her in my home games earlier, and that's with all the extra discarding I was doing.

posts.name: bolnerap
posts.cooked:
Blackfang, I can type up some tips or my whole route if you like. 

I actually had a fairly good time with this one, did it on my lunch hour today. Everyone finished in double-digit HP except Writhe and Mainstay, who were both in the 8-9 range. Everyone except Mainstay made good contributions:

- Dr. Medico healed a ton with Hippocratic Oath (I chose that with the early-game Unique Capabilities), Writhe kept stacking LC's deck after I removed her ability to play two cards a turn such that the ship never came back, and Idealist did tons of damage

- Unity kept Cryo Bot out for some great AOE damage

- Expat had a great time with Hairtrigger Reflexes and eventually got her Shotgun out

- Parse just generally wrecked stuff and gave us damage boosts. Never saw Extrasensory Awareness, that would have been keen.

- The two Phosphorescent Chambers from the environment helped us a lot more than they hurt us.

- I saw Mabel 3 times, L'epeiste twice, and everyone else once. LC flipped and flipped back, and then we burned her down.
